page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-2 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine belonging to the n4 server family. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel core with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The instance is configured with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, and does not bundle complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The underlying Intel processor includes an extensive set of advanced instruction extensions. Notably, it supports Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX, AVX512f, AVX512_vnni, AVX_vnni, AVX512_bf16) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX tile and AMX int8), which accelerate vector and matrix operations. Cryptographic acceleration is provided via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI flags, while integer operations are aided by BMI2, ADX, and FMA.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear single-core versus multi-core tradeoff. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the average category. However, multi-core and memory performance present significant limitations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Passmark memory scores are categorized as poor, and memory bandwidth tests show low throughput, with large block read-only speeds at 17.81 GB/sec and write speeds at 11.0 GB/sec. Similarly, database operations and software compilation benchmarks register in the poor tier, while static web serving throughput is weak at 3.68 GB/sec.

Given its hardware profile, the n4-highcpu-2 offers an entry-level compute-focused configuration. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for lightweight, single-threaded compute tasks that can leverage its advanced instruction sets without demanding high memory capacity or high multi-core throughput. Appropriate workloads include lightweight web serving, simple text processing, single-threaded utility scripts, and minor background tasks. It is not suited for memory-intensive databases, heavy multi-threaded compilation, or large-scale data processing.
description: The Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-2 is an x86_64 virtual machine featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs on a single physical Intel core and 4.0 GB of RAM. Lacking local storage and GPUs, this instance relies on its Intel processor's advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), to accelerate specific vector and matrix operations. Performance benchmarks reveal a distinct tradeoff: while single-core CPU and text processing capabilities are average, multi-core performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations are weak to poor. Consequently, this server is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded compute tasks, basic cryptography, and low-traffic web serving, rather than memory-intensive or highly parallelized enterprise workloads.
